newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on professional sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on professional sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended down on Monday from New York's Friday close after small amounts of professional selling in gloomy trade, gold dealers said.
"Mostly it was small amounts of professional selling," said one dealer at an international bank.

One bullion trader reported liquidation of long positions from Japanese traders from the Tokyo Commodity Exchange. Some dealers reported selling in pre-opening trade, noting it was most likely Australian producer selling.
Gold prices remained practically motionless in the afternoon, dealers said.
Physical demand was said healthy by some but speculative selling pressure was stronger, precious metals sources said.
Bullion ended at US$368.00/50 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$368.45/95 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$6 lower at HK$3,401 a tael.
Tael gold was trading at a premium to spot gold, with the U.S. dollar equivalent at $368.70/369.20.
"People were selling small amounts of tael and buying loco London," said one bullion trader.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society fell to -6.00 from its previous fix at -5.49.
